column12: IT READS HIGH BY ONE FILTER AND SAYS SO. NCT06568939 requires that a patient 'must have progressed on at least 1 line of prior therapy for locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC', and no line-of-therapy attrition is applied here, because no free US source gives the share of advanced EGFR-wild-type non-squamous NSCLC patients who reach a second line. The book's nearest figure, 60.638% going to a second line after first-line osimertinib (Kodama et al., Thorac Cancer 2025, doi 10.1111/1759-7714.70192), is a Japanese EGFR-mutant cohort and does not transfer. Applying something near it would cut this row by about 40%. The 23.6% is measured in submitted trial-screening samples rather than a population registry, so it carries submission bias

column11: THE c-Met HIGH HALF, AND THE TWO THRESHOLDS ARE WHY. The label covers only the high expressers: 'EMRELIS is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic, non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with high c-Met protein overexpression [>=50% of tumor cells with strong (3+) staining], as determined by an FDA-approved test ... who have received a prior systemic therapy' (DailyMed setid bc04f980-3957-4e35-ab81-8ec2ffe87215, SPL version 3, effective 2025-07-10, the Emrelis row in the book's labels table; accelerated approval 2025-05-14, BLA 761384, openFDA). NCT06568939 enrols at HALF that threshold: 'Must have c-Met overexpressing non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (defined as >= 25% tumor cells with 3+ staining (high [>= 50% 3+]; intermediate [>= 25% - < 50%]) as assessed by a Sponsor designated immunohistochemistry (IHC) laboratory' (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, protocol M25-274, read 2026-11-14). So the enrolled population is the union of a labelled half and an unlabelled half, and the labelled half's share of it is measured by the same LUMINOSITY prescreen the eligible row uses: 13.5% c-Met high over 23.6% c-Met overexpressing = 0.572034
column12: what the readout actually decides is the c-Met INTERMEDIATE stratum, 10.1% of nonsquamous EGFR-wild-type NSCLC (23.6 less 13.5; the subtraction is mine, no source states the intermediate share directly). That is 0.427966 of this layer, about 7,030 patients a year. Two cautions. LUMINOSITY's own response rates split across exactly this boundary, 34.6% in c-Met high against 22.9% in c-Met intermediate, so the unlabelled half is the weaker half. And the registry discloses no cap or stratification on the high/intermediate split, so the realised enrolment mix is not knowable from the record

column11: the share both other AbbVie NSCLC seeds carry, abbv_abbv_1480.csv and abbv_telisotuzumab_adizutecan.csv: 'a share of the pool above, set against what the molecule has to displace'. What it has to displace here is docetaxel, which NCT06568939 excludes by prior exposure ('Received prior docetaxel therapy' is an exclusion), so the trial is positioning teliso-V ahead of the second-line chemotherapy standard rather than after it
column12: A JUDGEMENT, not a measurement, and it errs high: NCT06568939 is a dose-optimisation study (six of its seven primary outcomes are toxicity measures, only 'Objective Response (OR) by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR)' is efficacy), so the readout buys a dose rather than an indication, and the c-Met intermediate stratum it would open is the one with the 22.9% response rate. Against that, teliso-V is already approved and stocked for the high expressers, so the prescriber, the IHC assay and the reimbursement path all exist before the intermediate label arrives
